phonology.name: English (General American)
phonology.notation: ARPAbet, cmusphinx/cmudict master working copy (post-0.7b); stress digits 0/1/2 on vowel phones
phonology.prominence_rule: lexical stress from CMUdict (1 or 2 -> prominent, 0 -> not), with the harness's WEAK_ALWAYS / WEAK_NONFINAL function-word demotion applied at the phrase level -- doctrine 46: a function-word list is part of a phonology, not an optimisation
phonology.relation: none declared. An English pair is judged in every relation it stands in -- each coarse relation (score()) and every registry schema (quality/relations.py REGISTRY) -- so `rhymes()` stays the inherited stub and the channels decide -- see this module's docstring
phonology.source: cmusphinx/cmudict master working copy, md5 5837aa6e49fd070d482b8ca0525f28ef; BSD-2-clause (Carnegie Mellon University), NOT public domain; see data/sources.tsv
phonology.fallback_licenses: no fallback: a word CMUdict cannot read REFUSES

poem_pronunciation_realization.AH: AH0 retains schwa; AH1/AH2 retain STRUT. Normalized on lexical parses before function-word prominence demotion.
poem_pronunciation_realization.before_r: Native LH.Declaration.nucleus_licence_before_r; IH/IY agree only when the syllable coda starts R.
poem_pronunciation_realization.lexical_stress: Retained separately from the editorial metrical/prominence grid.

of.source: Cambridge US /əv/ in auction of promises; https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/pronunciation/english/auction-of-promises

darkest.source: Compositional declaration: CMUdict dark D AA1 R K plus Cambridge US -est /ɪst/; https://dictionary.cambridge.org/pronunciation/english/est

method.judge: Existing quality.relations.pair_satisfies_any over every original occurrence pair, using the same pronunciation scope and normalization as the matching complete E1–E22 base.

E1.description: Both anchors must actually be stressed; equal weak stress is insufficient.

E7.description: Compare the complete aligned tails; unmatched syllables cannot disappear.

E11.description: Require complete aligned tails and the native manner-class agreement on all post-vowel consonants, including post-anchor onsets and the empty class.

E12.description: The complete rime must acquire terminal consonants, with all preceding rime material unchanged.

E13.description: The complete rime must lose terminal consonants, with all preceding rime material unchanged.

E14.description: The complete post-vocalic cluster of the shorter first word must prefix the longer second word's cluster.

E15.description: The complete post-vocalic cluster of the shorter second word must prefix the longer first word's cluster.

E18.description: Compare the actual final syllable of each word and require both to be unstressed.

E19.description: Reverse the complete second word's phone sequence exactly once; do not reverse its syllable order beforehand.

method.analysis: All positive observed categories are retained regardless of the schema's writing-quality status. No lyric revision or preference filtering is applied.
method.E63: Native homoioteleuton schema with English.resources (quality.morphology.ENG_RESOURCES): final nucleus, coda and prominence agree; declared affix agrees; tokens differ. The existing bound-pair route removes placement only.
method.E66: Native trite rhyme schema: sound agreement plus the declared 30-pair CLICHE_PAIRS partition; no frequency threshold or invented extension. Bound-pair scope includes internal words.
method.H1: Native Reviser.earned_pair_ban HOMEOTELEUTON observation, using its stress-anchored _spelled_rimes; asked only for distinct words with an existing nonabsence tail-sound match and an equal nonempty spelled rime. Candidate ranking and the modal-frequency tier are never invoked.
method.absence_flags: E63 raw positives based on two empty declared affixes are retained but marked absence-only; absence of an affix is not displayed as an actual shared ending.
method.pronunciation: All General American dictionary readings with the recorded vowel-quality normalization. A pair's ID set is the union across supported whole readings: different IDs need not hold in one simultaneous performance. Compact witnesses retain reading-dependent support.
method.spelling_anchor: H1 uses the existing Reviser lexicon-based stress anchor exactly; sound support is inherited from the matched pair in the selected reading population.
method.H1_witnesses: Existing positive reading witnesses for qualifying tail-sound labels are carried to H1 without inventing or re-running a pronunciation.

reading_witnesses: promises = P R AA1 M IH0 S IH0 Z
promises = P R AA1 M IH0 S IH0 Z

category_notes.E63: Matching final sound and a shared ending in Codex Musica's declared morphology resource. This heuristic identifies ending forms; it does not guarantee a word's contextual grammatical analysis.
category_notes.E66: A matching sound pair on Codex Musica's declared trite-rhyme list. List membership is shown as an observation; the list does not exhaust familiar rhymes.
category_notes.H1: An existing sound match with the same spelled ending from the native rhyming stress anchor. Separate from the shared-affix figure; repeated identical words keep their repetition label.
